correctness.rationale: For n=2^a q^b, the normalized 2-part exponential-unitary sum is odd while the normalized q-part is 1 modulo q, forcing the exact split A=q^(b-1), B=2^a. The product of the corresponding normalized ratios equals 2; a geometric bound gives S_a>4/3, while proper divisors of a are at most a/2, eliminating every a except 2 and 4. Exact resolution of those cases leaves only 36. Edge cases and a standalone bounded computation were also checked.

originality.rationale: The 1971 indexed abstract, the 2011 primary paper, the classical 1978 e-perfect analogue as summarized in a standard handbook, current OEIS records, a 2025 paper using e-unitary terminology, synonymous searches, and the current SCOPE archive were checked. No located source states the two-prime e-unitary perfect classification. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from older variant terminology and incomplete direct access to two historical sources.

value.rationale: The theorem closes the complete two-prime-support case for e-unitary perfect numbers and shows that any counterexample to the open implication from e-unitary perfect to e-perfect must involve at least three distinct primes. It also supplies the e-unitary analogue of the classical two-prime e-perfect classification by a short direct argument.
